questions.stem:
The graph shown below is based roughly on data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture: food production in South Asia, as an index (100 during 1969-71), against the year, from 1975 to just after 1981.

During which intervals did food production decrease in South Asia?

figures.alt: A smooth curve of the food production index against year, from 1975 to about 1981.4. Vertical axis (index) marks at 110, 115 and 120; horizontal axis marks at 1975, 1977, 1979 and 1981. Dashed vertical lines drop from the curve at 1976, 1977, 1978, 1979, 1980 and 1981. The curve starts near 113 in 1975, falls to a local minimum near 110.5 at 1976, rises through about 115 at 1977 (steepest here), reaches a local maximum near 122 at 1978, falls through about 118 at 1979, reaches a local minimum near 115 at 1980, then rises through about 119 at 1981 and keeps rising to about 123. The curve bends upward (concave up) from the start to 1977 and from 1979 to the end, and downward from 1977 to 1979.

figures.alt: A smooth curve of the food production index against year, from 1975 to about 1981.4. Vertical axis (index) marks at 110, 115 and 120; horizontal axis marks at 1975, 1977, 1979 and 1981. Dashed vertical lines drop from the curve at 1976, 1977, 1978, 1979, 1980 and 1981. The curve starts near 113 in 1975, falls to a local minimum near 110.5 at 1976, rises through about 115 at 1977 (steepest here), reaches a local maximum near 122 at 1978, falls through about 118 at 1979, reaches a local minimum near 115 at 1980, then rises through about 119 at 1981 and keeps rising to about 123. The curve bends upward (concave up) from the start to 1977 and from 1979 to the end, and downward from 1977 to 1979.
